Tesco (tesco.com) tracking config fragments — reference copy only, loaded by nothing. To use, paste the arrays into a study config under tracking.* (contract: docs/config-schema.md §3.1/§3.2; guides: docs/README.md → 'Semantic-group (sg) rules' and 'Force-tracked elements'). Tesco's 2026 DDS-web (CSS-modules) build renders product tiles with two different components, so there is one sg rule per markup variant — the variants' selectors are disjoint, so whichever isn't present on a page is inert. (1) Carousel / recommendation tile (homepage, 'you may also like' rails):
— the tile stamps the clean name on its own aria-label (first source), the h2 title link text is the fallback, and the tile's data-testid (product_) is the last resort. The tile also holds a nested attribute-less
around promotions + buybox; closest() walks past it to the outer tile. (2) Listing / search grid tile (groceries, browse, search — ul[data-testid='dynamic-grid'] > li):
  • with no data-product-id or aria-label, so the container is identified by the product-tile heading it contains (:has) and named from that heading's link text, then any h2 product link, then the bare numeric data-testid. Quantity controls (shown once a product is in the trolley) come in two markups too, so there is one trio of entries per variant: the carousel tile uses the design-system component (ddsweb-quantity-controls-* data-auto buttons, count in .ddsweb-quantity-controls__subtext); the grid/listing tile (and the same product-tile component rendered outside a grid) uses the BEM buybox classes (online-components-product-tile-buybox-increment/decrement-button__button, count in ...-buybox-quantity__label). Either way: +/- → quantity_add / quantity_remove — the buttons have no text, so eV is their aria-label, e.g. 'add 1 ' / 'remove 1 from trolley', which the tag falls back to for icon-only controls; the count → quantity with eV '3', re-rendered by Tesco on each change so a fresh appear carries the new count.
